verdict: No leads in 20 days; the gap is intake coverage, not ad performance.
narrative: You received 10 tracked leads over the last 28 days at a cost of $255.52 per lead — and zero of those leads arrived in the final 20 days of the period. The data points to an intake coverage gap as the primary blocker: your pipeline shows 66 opportunities created this period against only 10 attributed ad leads, meaning a significant volume of phone and Local Services calls is arriving but not being counted in the lead total. Google Ads spend also pulled back sharply in the last week, averaging $68 per day versus a higher prior pace, which is being reviewed alongside budget allocation across channels. Conversion tracking is being repaired so this figure more accurately reflects actual lead volume going forward. Once intake coverage is confirmed and attribution is corrected, the reported lead count and cost per lead should reflect what is actually happening in your business.
